title: PHARM · Diphenhydramine in older adults (CONFUSES, NOT SNOOZES) (high stakes, night shift)
hook: Nurses: 84 and can't sleep at 2 AM. Diphenhydramine?
hook_backups: Nurses: a 'harmless' sleep aid. Then she fell.

belief: Diphenhydramine is a harmless sleep aid.

story.patient: 84-year-old woman, day 2 after hip fracture surgery
story.order: diphenhydramine 25 to 50 mg by mouth at bedtime as needed for sleep

timeline.mistake: MISTAKE 1 · a strong anticholinergic for an 84-year-old

timeline.beat: Never screens for delirium, never checks pain, bladder or oxygen

caught_it: New confusion at night: screen for delirium, look for the cause
Check pain, a full bladder, oxygen, glasses and hearing aids

memory_line: In older adults, diphenhydramine confuses, not snoozes.
caption_lesson:
🌙 Night shift, 2:00 AM. She's 84, day 2 after hip fracture surgery.
• Restless, awake, asking where she is
• PRN (as-needed) order: diphenhydramine for sleep

❌ 3 mistakes
1️⃣ Gave diphenhydramine 50 mg to an 84-year-old
2️⃣ Never screened for delirium or looked for the cause
3️⃣ Bed high, bed alarm off
➡️ 3:35 AM: pulling at her IV, seeing bugs, bladder full. She falls and hits her head. Rapid response.

💊 Diphenhydramine in older adults (CONFUSES, NOT SNOOZES)
• Strongly anticholinergic: blocks a brain and body messenger (acetylcholine)
• Can cause confusion, delirium, urine retention, constipation, dry mouth, blurry vision and falls
• On the AGS (American Geriatrics Society) Beers Criteria: avoid in older adults

⚠️ New confusion at night is not "just sundowning"
• Think delirium until proven otherwise
• Look for the cause: pain, a full bladder, low oxygen, infection, new medicines

✅ The right move
• Screen for delirium, check pain, bladder and oxygen
• Glasses and hearing aids on, lights low, quiet, reorient her
• Low bed, bed alarm on
• Call the provider about the sleep order

🧠 In older adults, diphenhydramine confuses, not snoozes.
